title: Modular GPU probe plugin and warmup optimization to reduce service startup latency
creator: Alicia Chen
description: Problem: Service cold start includes a monolithic GPU ABI probe and kernel loader that runs several heavyweight checks (CUDA runtime version, driver symbols, CUTLASS compatibility matrix, Triton ABI probe) serially. This causes tail latency and increases instance warmup time, especially across heterogenous fleets where some nodes need fallbacks. Goal: Refactor the probe into a modular plugin architecture with lazy loading, per-arch probe caching, and an opt-in warmup path that runs prioritized lightweight checks first and defers expensive validations to a background plugin worker. Deliverables: 1) Probe plugin framework with a stable interface for third-party kernel adapters; 2) Probe cache (TTL + per-GPU model) persisted to disk to avoid repeated cold probes; 3) Parallel prioritized probe execution (fast sanity checks first, heavy compatibility checks later); 4) Safe canary rollout and automatic fallback to precomputed compatibility map if runtime probe fails or exceeds latency SLO. Success metrics: reduce median cold-start probe latency from ~320ms to <120ms and 95th percentile from >900ms to <300ms in mixed fleets, reduce pod readiness flaps during rollout, and simplify adding new CUTLASS/Triton adapters.
comments: 2025-01-16 - Alicia Chen: Spiked on prototype plugin API; defined ProbePlugin {name, priority, run(context)->(status, metadata)} and lightweight ProbeCoordinator that schedules plugins by priority. Confirmed no kernel symbols are accessed until a plugin runs in our prototype. Initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Modular+GPU+Probe+Design

2025-01-22 - Raghu Malhotra: Benchmarked serial probe vs prototype parallel probe on mixed fleet (p4d + a100): serial median 320ms, 95p 940ms. Prototype median 85ms, 95p 210ms with conservative parallelism. Observed one flaky node where driver probing blocked for 3s — we should add a probe timeout and fallback to disk cache.

2025-01-28 - Priya Nair (PM): Prioritize conservative rollout. Request adding telemetry events (probe_start, probe_plugin_complete, probe_cache_hit) and a console dashboard. Also add a feature flag to disable background heavy checks per deployment.

2025-02-03 - Raghu Malhotra: Implemented persistent probe cache (boltDB) keyed by driver + cuda + gpu_uuid and TTL 24h. Local experiments show cache hit reduces probe cost to ~15ms on warm nodes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428

2025-02-08 - QA: Integration test failures in the on-prem packaging path where SELinux restricted access to the cache file. Created followup ENG-90133 to add secure directory and selinux policy notes.

2025-02-10 - Alicia Chen: Introduced plugin-level timeouts and a 'fast-path' composed of (cuda-runtime-check, basic-kernel-symbols, minimal-cutlass-sm-check). Heavy checks (quant-loader-compat, exhaustive-cutlass-version-run) moved to background with a throttled queue. Added feature gate runtime.probe.mode = [eager, lazy, cached].
2025-02-15 - Observability: Added probe metrics to statsd - probe.latency_ms, probe.plugin.latency_ms, probe.cache.hit boolean. Initial dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/probe-warmup

2025-02-18 - Raghu Malhotra: Canary rollout initiated on 10% of Dedicated GPU pool with rollback policy if probe.latency 95p > 300ms for 15m. No regressions observed. Filed small followup to tune TTL per-region (ENG-90140).
notes: Tradeoffs: lazy heavy checks improve startup but can surface compatibility issues later; mitigations include safe fallback map and conservative canary. Rollback plan: toggle runtime.probe.mode to cached and force-drop cache to revert to previous behavior. Long-term: plugin marketplace for vendor adapters and signing of adapter metadata.
